sum/inputs: A neuron takes in a vector, x. This one has two entries: two and one.
sum/weights: It keeps one weight per entry, w, here one and minus three, and multiplies each input by its weight.
sum/sum: Then it adds up the products, plus a bias, b, of two. Two, minus three, plus two: one. That sum, w dot x plus b, is the pre-activation.
sum/relu: Last comes the bend, the activation. Here it is a ReLU: it keeps a positive number and turns a negative one into zero. One is positive, so the neuron outputs one.
sum/neg: Feed it one and two instead. One, minus six, plus two is minus three, and the ReLU turns that into zero. The neuron stays silent.
bend/linear: Before the bend, w dot x plus b is exactly a class score from a linear classifier. Across the inputs, it rises steadily in one direction and falls in the other.
bend/line: It is zero along a straight line. Every input on one side scores above zero, and every input on the other side below.
bend/half: The ReLU flattens the negative side to zero. So a neuron splits its inputs with a line: silent on one side, and growing with the distance on the other. A linear classifier with a bend.
bend/bias: The weights set which way the line faces, and the bias slides it. With a bias of zero, the line would have to pass through the origin.
